description: A customer is experiencing issues with an application that uses an SQLite database located at /home/user/appdata/diagnostics.db. As a support engineer, your task is to collect basic diagnostic information about this database using the SQLite CLI tools. Please do the following: 1. Use the SQLite command-line interface to query the database file at /home/user/appdata/diagnostics.db. 2. Retrieve the list of all tables in the database. 3. For each table found, obtain the row count and the names of all columns (schema information). 4. Save your diagnostics in a text file called /home/user/diagnostics_report.txt. The format must be as follows: - The first line must be: "Diagnostics for /home/user/appdata/diagnostics.db" - For each table, output: - The table name (one line, in the format: "Table: <tablename>") - The column names, comma-separated (one line, in the format: "Columns: col1,col2,...") - The row count (one line, in the format: "Row count: <number>") - Separate each table section by a blank line. Example output (where there are two tables, "users" and "logs"): Diagnostics for /home/user/appdata/diagnostics.db Table: users Columns: id,name,email Row count: 5 Table: logs Columns: id,user_id,message,timestamp Row count: 10 Make sure: - The file /home/user/diagnostics_report.txt is correctly formatted with precise information as described above. - All information must be gathered directly from the SQLite database using CLI tools.
